name: Aneurysm of Sinus of Valsalva

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No standardized formal criteria; diagnosis based on imaging and clinical presentation

criteria.description: Visualization of aneurysmal dilation of one or more sinuses of Valsalva on echocardiography, CT, or MRI
Evidence of rupture into cardiac chambers or pericardium causing shunt or tamponade
Symptoms such as acute chest pain, dyspnea, or heart failure signs consistent with aneurysm or rupture

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Imaging evidence of aneurysm with or without clinical symptoms; rupture signs increase diagnostic certainty
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis primarily relies on imaging modalities; surgical findings may confirm diagnosis

pathognomonic.symptomName: Dilatation of the sinus of Valsalva

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) in heart failure
Possible inflammatory markers if endocarditis present
imaging: Transthoracic and transesophageal echocardiography showing aneurysmal dilation
CT angiography or cardiac MRI confirming size and rupture
Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly or pulmonary congestion
genetic: Associations with connective tissue disorders such as Marfan syndrome or Ehlers-Danlos syndrome in some cases
other: Hemodynamic assessment via cardiac catheterization if needed

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of aneurysmal dilation of sinus of Valsalva
Diffuse aortic root enlargement without localized sinus aneurysm
Usually associated with connective tissue disorders

redFlags: Sudden onset chest pain with continuous murmur indicating rupture
Signs of acute heart failure or cardiogenic shock
New onset severe dyspnea or hypotension
references: Moustafa S, et al. Sinus of Valsalva aneurysms—47 years of a single center experience and systematic overview of published reports. Am J Cardiol. 2007.
Takach TJ, et al. Sinus of Valsalva aneurysm or fistula: management and outcome. Ann Thorac Surg. 1999.
